cycles.explanation: Miami, Ohio State, Ole Miss, Georgia, Texas, Texas A&M, Notre Dame, Virginia, Louisville and NC State form a loop: following every head-to-head result among them leads back to where it started, so no ordering can honour all 14 of them. The weakest link was Louisville's 24-21 win over Miami (+5.5 adjusted margin; the winner rates 12.2 points worse by FPI; the loser fared better against 3 shared opponents), so it was set aside, along with 1 other result in this loop.

Texas Tech, BYU, Utah, SMU, Iowa State, TCU, Houston, Arizona and Arizona State form a loop: following every head-to-head result among them leads back to where it started, so no ordering can honour all 19 of them. The weakest link was Arizona State's 26-22 win over Texas Tech (a 4-point win at home is worth +1.5 once venue is accounted for; the winner rates 15.2 points worse by FPI; the loser fared better against 3 shared opponents), so it was set aside, along with 3 other results in this loop.

USC, Michigan, Washington and Illinois form a loop: following every head-to-head result among them leads back to where it started, so no ordering can honour all 4 of them. The weakest link was Illinois's 34-32 win over USC (a 2-point win at home is worth -0.5 once venue is accounted for; the winner rates 8.0 points worse by FPI; the loser fared better against 2 shared opponents), so it was set aside.

Navy, South Florida and North Texas form a loop: following every head-to-head result among them leads back to where it started, so no ordering can honour all 3 of them. The weakest link was North Texas's 31-17 win over Navy (+11.5 adjusted margin), so it was set aside.

source.attribution: Data: CollegeFootballData.com (FPI, Strength of Record and Strength of Schedule via ESPN)

stages: Stage 1 - rank every team by what it has achieved and how good it is: 0.75 x Strength of Record + 0.25 x FPI rank (all national ranks, lower is better).
Stage 2 - adjust for how your losses actually look: the venue and margin of each defeat, the quality of your best win, and how comfortably you win.
Stage 3 - when a result spans more than 15 places, pull both teams 0.5 of the way to their midpoint; the upset says both were mis-rated.
Stage 4 - reorder so as few head-to-head results as possible are contradicted, weighing each result by how convincing it was against how far a team would have to move.
Stage 5 - report every contradiction loop and every overridden result, so nothing is hidden.
methodology.summary: base = 0.75 x SoR + 0.25 x FPI; pool 40; H2H strength 14, drift exponent 1.5; upset regression on (gap 15, 0.5)
